notice-kreyol-sounds.label: Notice Kreyòl Sounds
notice-kreyol-sounds.summary: Start reading Kreyòl by noticing dependable spelling patterns, meaningful accent marks, the spelling ou, and the common nasal patterns an, en, and on.

sound-choice-accent.title: Spot the accent
sound-choice-accent.prompt: Which Kreyòl word keeps a meaningful accent mark in its standard spelling?
sound-choice-accent.hint: Look for the spelling feature practiced in this lesson.

help.concept: Kreyòl spelling keeps meaningful vowel and sound patterns visible in the written word.
help.hint_1: Focus on the spelling pattern named in the lesson instead of applying English spelling habits.
help.hint_2: Compare the letters and accent marks carefully before choosing your response.

sound-fill-mesi.title: Complete mèsi
sound-fill-mesi.prompt: Choose the spelling that completes the Kreyòl word for thank you.
sound-fill-mesi.hint: Use the sound-spelling pattern from the lesson to complete the word.

help.concept: Kreyòl spelling keeps meaningful vowel and sound patterns visible in the written word.
help.hint_1: Focus on the spelling pattern named in the lesson instead of applying English spelling habits.
help.hint_2: Compare the letters and accent marks carefully before choosing your response.

sound-listen-bonjou.title: Hear bonjou
sound-listen-bonjou.prompt: Listen, then build the Kreyòl greeting you hear.
sound-listen-bonjou.hint: Replay the audio, then rebuild exactly what you hear.

help.concept: Listening practice connects the complete written Kreyòl phrase with the phrase you hear.
help.hint_1: Replay the phrase and keep the words in the same order.
help.hint_2: Listen for the whole word or phrase rather than trying to translate each sound into English spelling.

sound-speak-mesi.title: Say mèsi
sound-speak-mesi.prompt: Say the Kreyòl word shown: Mèsi.
sound-speak-mesi.hint: Read the Kreyòl target once, then say the whole phrase.

help.concept: Speaking practice checks the transcript of the phrase you say against the authored Kreyòl target.
help.hint_1: Say the complete target phrase clearly at a comfortable pace.
help.hint_2: Use the written Kreyòl as your guide; this activity checks the transcript, not a phoneme-level pronunciation score.

sound-build-bonjou-manman.title: Build a greeting
sound-build-bonjou-manman.prompt: Arrange the Kreyòl words to make “Hello, Mom.”
sound-build-bonjou-manman.hint: Build the complete Kreyòl phrase in natural order.

help.concept: Sentence building uses the same Kreyòl word order and spelling that appear in the target phrase.
help.hint_1: Start with the phrase you recognize, then place the remaining word or punctuation in its natural position.
help.hint_2: Read the complete result aloud once before checking it.

sound-write-pen.title: Write pen
sound-write-pen.prompt: Type the Kreyòl word for bread used to notice the written en pattern.
sound-write-pen.hint: Write the Kreyòl form exactly as it appears in the lesson.

help.concept: Accurate Kreyòl writing preserves the spelling patterns and meaningful accent marks shown in the lesson.
help.hint_1: Write the complete Kreyòl form, including any accent mark that belongs in the word.
help.hint_2: Check the vowel spelling one more time before submitting.

sound-map.title: Kreyòl spelling gives you useful sound clues
sound-map.bodyMarkdown:
Kreyòl is written with a standardized spelling system. For a beginner, the most useful habit is to **look at the Kreyòl spelling itself instead of guessing from English spelling**.

Start with a few anchor words:

- **bonjou** — hello
- **mèsi** — thank you
- **wi** — yes
- **non** — no

You do not need to memorize every sound today. First, notice that the same written pattern is meant to guide you consistently when the pattern appears again.

vowel-patterns.title: Accent marks and ou matter
vowel-patterns.bodyMarkdown:
Two details are especially useful in your first Kreyòl words:

- **è** is a real part of the spelling. In **mèsi**, keep the accent when you write the word.
- **ou** works together as one common sound pattern. You see it at the end of **bonjou**.

Do not silently replace **è** with plain **e**, and do not drop one of the letters in **ou**. The goal is to build accurate visual habits from the beginning.

nasal-patterns.title: Notice an, en, and on
nasal-patterns.bodyMarkdown:
Kreyòl also uses common nasal vowel spellings such as **an**, **en**, and **on**. For now, learn to recognize the written patterns in familiar words rather than trying to master every pronunciation rule at once.

Examples to notice:

- **manman** — mother
- **pen** — bread
- **non** — no

Later lessons can refine how these patterns behave in different words. In this first lesson, your job is simply to spot and preserve the spelling.
